findings.detail: On a case-insensitive filesystem, two absent destinations named Ledger.md and ledger.md pass both protections. Writing the ledger creates their shared file; writing the status then truncates it, replacing the ledger with the status line while render returns success. This recurs from round 1's record-destination alias class: existing hard links are now detected, but aliases between new destinations remain unchecked.
findings.evidence: The pathname comparison at lines 283–284 treats differently cased POSIX paths as distinct. The samefile checks at lines 286–290 run only when target.exists(), so both are skipped for absent destinations. The sequential write_text calls at lines 305 and 307 subsequently write the same file on a case-insensitive filesystem.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: new record destinations can still alias and overwrite each other

findings.detail: The documented green expectation accepts a unittest control whose selected test is skipped. Such a run exits zero and prints both 'Ran 1 test' and 'OK (skipped=1)', satisfying every supplied predicate. A control patch that introduces a skip can therefore receive control-green and be published without exercising the property, contrary to the explicit requirement that skipped controls fail publication.
findings.evidence: The example's green expectation contains only exit_code 0 and the substrings 'Ran 1 test' and 'OK'; its skip exclusion appears only under red. matches() accepts those substrings and defaults excludes to an empty list. Both the control verdict at checked-plant:199 and independent rendering at checked-plant:269–270 reuse this green expectation. The control regression uses a shell checker and never exercises framework skips.
findings.title: Absent or partial data: the documented green predicate publishes skipped controls

findings.detail: Normalized relative script names beginning with '-' are accepted by the manifest validator but passed directly where Bash still parses options. For example, declaring an existing -check.sh as check fails during Bash option parsing instead of executing that file. The same defect affects setup scripts and is repeated during restoration, so an otherwise valid campaign fails.
findings.evidence: relative() rejects absolute paths and empty, dot or parent components, but permits -check.sh. validate_manifest() then accepts it through membership in inputs. Both command vectors at lines 175 and 178 omit '--' before the manifest-supplied script path. The patch path is absolute and does not share this ambiguity; existing tests use check.sh and setup.sh.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: leading-dash script paths are interpreted as Bash options
